Subject: Stepwise remediation plan (draft) — legal & HR review

Team,

I have attached a first-pass remediation plan for Rohan Mehta (attached: PIP_template_v1.docx). Before I schedule an initial conversation with Rohan next week, I want to make sure the language and timeline are appropriate and that we have HR and legal aligned on next steps. High-level context: over the last two quarters Rohan's delivery has trended below expectations for his IC role on Search infra — repeated missed sprint commitments, two post-ship bug escalations, and limited participation in cross-team design reviews. I've documented examples in the draft under "Objective evidence".

What I need from you:
- Legal (Laura): please review the wording under "Possible outcomes" and flag any phrasing that could be interpreted as punitive or inconsistent with policy. Also advise if the 60-day timeline needs to be adjusted given the documented coaching already provided.
- HR (Monica/Marissa): confirm we have the right policy references included and that the support options (EAP, coaching) are listed. Please confirm whether we should treat this as a standard PIP vs. a performance improvement notice with escalated oversight.

Proposed timeline in the doc: 60 days total, weekly 1:1 check-ins, mid-point written summary, final review with manager + People Ops. I'm open to changing the cadence.

Attachments: PIP_template_v1.docx (editable), evidence_summary.zip (listed inside the doc, not attached here)

Thanks — I want to move carefully here and avoid surprises for Rohan while preserving a clear record.

—Kim

Kim — thanks for the context and the draft. I skimmed PIP_template_v1 and left inline comments in Drive (link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cPIPGuidelines). A few immediate notes: 

- Please add quantifiable success criteria where possible (e.g., "complete 3 code reviews per sprint" is better than "improve code quality").
- Replace any "last chance" language — we want to avoid implying immediate termination; focus on outcomes and supports.
- Add a short accommodations checkbox for known disabilities or temporary life events, and reference the accommodation process.
- Confirm with People Ops whether we should include the employee in the evidence packet at meeting time or keep it for internal review first.

I'll attach our canonical policy PDF and the People Ops checklist. See attached: policy-PIP-guidelines.pdf. We can also offer the external coaching partner (people-partners@consulting.co) if you want structured weekly coaching; I cc'd them on the participant list in case you prefer to loop them in later.

If you want, I'll slot a 30-min calibration meeting for 11/03 10:00-10:30 to align manager/HR/legal before you meet Rohan.

- Monica

Kim/Monica — quick legal read here. I appreciate the careful framing. Inline/high-level redlines below; I can send an annotated doc if helpful.

1) Outcomes language — remove any references that could be seen as "guaranteed termination." Replace "failure to meet the requirements will result in termination" with "failure to achieve the agreed objectives may lead to further employment action up to and including termination, subject to People Ops review." This reduces absolute framing while preserving escalation.
2) Timeline — 60 days is acceptable for the scope you described, but if there have already been prior formal coaching steps documented, consider a 45-day window with a documented mid-point.
3) Evidence & transparency — include a clause that the employee will receive the PIP document and supporting examples prior to the meeting. This reduces surprise claims.
4) Data retention — ensure PIP documentation is stored in the People Ops secure folder with access logs. I've added a note about retention (7 years) and audit hooks.

I recommend we do one of the following before sending to Rohan: 1) a short calibration meeting (15–30m) with manager + HR to agree phrasing; or 2) if you want to move faster, I can prepare an annotated version with legal redlines and send it to Monica for People Ops finalization.

Forwarding the original for context below.
